overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes of six meetings. It rejected the Board's argument that the complaint was untimely, since the minutes obligation is continuing. The Board had already approved and posted the minutes, so no further remedial action was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve minutes of meetings held since February 28, with eight sets listed as pending on its July 18 notice.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve meeting minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
